items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

ctx.x: I always tried to tell a story with an album. You put the needle on one side, turn it over, needle on, it was a story. Because people did really listen top to bottom, which is a lost art now because everybody listens to a track here or a track there. They download a track or they stream a track, but not an album. It used to be the album had to tell a story musically. It had to be. Going back to when Sinatra started doing that stuff with Nelson Riddle in the 50s. Those were concept albums. Probably the first…
good. Mitch Miller in New York. But when he got with Capitol in LA and especially with Nelson Riddle and Axel Stordahl and oh the great trumpet player.
